item.title: Trump Hits Campaign Trail as White House Turmoil Weighs on GOP Midterm Prospects
item.description: As Trump held rallies around the nation, his White House was consumed by dramas that reinforce how his presidency has become a drag on his party’s prospects in the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager
item.media:description: President Trump arriving in West Palm Beach, Fla., after giving remarks at a midterm election campaign rally in Highland Heights, Ky., on Saturday.

item.title: Trump Outlines Rapid Plan to Close and Overhaul D.C. Golf Course
item.description: The plan to begin work transforming the course in four weeks injected fresh urgency into a federal lawsuit opposing changes to East Potomac Golf Links.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Andrew Leyden for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Trump administration removed hundreds of trees from East Potomac Golf Links earlier this month, drawing a rebuke from a federal judge.

item.title: O.J. Simpson, a Secret Informant and a Decades-Old Mystery
item.description: An “extremely reliable” informant told authorities about the missing murder weapon, according to newly unsealed records. The informant’s brother told The Times his sibling was at the crime scene.
item.dc:creator: Mike Baker and Tim Arango
item.media:description: During his 1995 double-murder trial, O.J. Simpson wore the gloves found at the crime scene and his home.

item.title: 5 Takeaways From The Times’s Re-Examination of the O.J. Simpson Case
item.description: Newly unsealed court files and interviews challenge the popular narrative around the murders and the “trial of the century.”
item.dc:creator: Mike Baker and Tim Arango
item.media:description: O.J. Simpson, center, during his double murder trial in Los Angeles in 1995.

item.title: June 17, 1994: Millions Watched Police Chase O.J. Simpson in a Bronco
item.description: The chase occurred days after his ex-wife and her friend were killed. New details shed light on the role that a mobster might have played in helping Mr. Simpson.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales
item.media:description: On June 17, 1994, the police engaged in a televised, slow-speed pursuit of a white Bronco carrying O.J. Simpson, who was being charged with two murders.

item.title: Trump Defends Plans to Ease Russia Sanctions and Hints at a Hostage Deal
item.description: The president on Sunday justified his reversal of almost five years of sanctions against Russia as part of peace negotiations. He did not name any hostage.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger
item.media:description: President Trump wrote on social media on Sunday: “I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.”

item.title: Zelensky Says Trump Risks ‘Historic Mistake’ If He Backs Russia
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine pressed Sunday for more information on possible restrictions to Starshield, a U.S.-provided satellite internet service used by the Ukrainian military.
item.dc:creator: Constant Méheut
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine in Brussels on Friday.

item.title: Larry David Mocks the D.S.A. Some Are Not Amused.
item.description: The comedian satirized the Democratic Socialists of America, its platform and its opposition to Israel in an essay that some did not LOL at.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer and Evan Gorelick
item.media:description: The comedian Larry David spoofed the Democratic Socialists of America in a satire in which he imagined joining the organization and shaping its manifesto with new proposals.

item.title: 2028 Presidential ‘Shadow Primary’ Descends on the Midterm Elections
item.description: The schedule is especially packed in New Hampshire, an early presidential nominating state where there is a competitive Senate race Democrats are flocking to this month.
item.dc:creator: Evan Gorelick
item.media:description: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California taking the stage during a campaign event for Representative Chris Pappas, the Democratic Senate nominee, in Exeter, N.H., on Saturday.

item.title: Some MAHA Voters in Arizona Question Their G.O.P. Ties
item.description: MAHA’s alliance with MAGA had energized voters to support President Trump’s 2024 campaign. Now, some aren’t so sure.
item.dc:creator: Sejal Govindarao
item.media:credit: Adriana Zehbrauskas for The New York Times
item.media:description: Patrick Sullivan Jr. and Ashley Leroux Sullivan, the owners of Firefly Coffee, are looking for candidates that have a strong MAHA platform.

item.title: Talarico Kicks Off Campaign Tour of Texas as Senate Election Looms
item.description: The Democratic candidate invoked a rallying cry from the TV show “Friday Night Lights” as he began his final campaign push before the Nov. 3 election.
item.dc:creator: Jesus Jiménez
item.media:description: James Talarico speaking in Plano, Texas, the first stop on his campaign tour, on Sunday.

item.title: Gas Prices Soar to Over $10 a Gallon at This California Outpost
item.description: Drive along a meandering highway through Big Sur, and you could happen upon this roadside stop. Maybe you won’t notice the prices.
item.dc:creator: Corina Knoll and Brandon Tauszik

item.title: France in Shock After Protests Turn Into Riots, Damaging Buildings and Shops
item.description: After anti-government protests devolved into chaos, leaders from across the political spectrum blamed one another for the unrest, even as it largely subsided on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Porter and Ségolène Le Stradic
item.media:description: A street in Paris, littered on Sunday with debris a day after nationwide protests and riots.

item.title: The French City of Limoges Wasn’t Known for Unrest. Then Rioters Set Fire to Its City Hall.
item.description: As unrest surged across France this weekend, the most surprising attack came in the quiet city of Limoges, where rioters set fire to the city hall.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Imbert
item.media:description: The city hall in Limoges on Saturday night. The violence in the city, better known for its porcelain than its politics, was among the most surprising episodes of France’s widespread unrest.

item.title: Why Are There Protests in France?
item.description: Rioters attacked city halls and shops over the weekend amid protests over living costs and poor school conditions.
item.dc:creator: Amelia Nierenberg, Lynsey Chutel and Catherine Porter
item.media:description: Forensic officers examine the tourist office in Lyon, France.

item.title: Finding a Foothold for a Growing Network of Deportees in Jamaica
item.description: A nonprofit in Jamaica is helping a growing network of deportees from the U.S. find a foothold in their country of origin.
item.dc:creator: Gabriella Angotti-Jones and Lisa Armstrong
item.media:description: Alvin McLean at the headquarters of the Family Unification & Resettlement Initiative

item.title: Migrants From Ukraine and Sudan to Keep Deportation Protections for Now
item.description: Temporary Protected Status for the two countries was set to expire on Monday. The Trump administration said an announcement would be made “at the appropriate time.”
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Valerie Plesch for The New York Times
item.media:description: The decision to hold off on an announcement about Ukrainian and Sudanese migrants mirrored a similar move by the Trump administration last month to allow people from El Salvador to keep their deportation protections for now.

item.title: Strong Exports Stabilize China’s Economic Growth in Official Statistics
item.description: A prolonged housing crash, sluggish consumer spending and plunging investment have left China dependent on exports to keep the economy growing.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher
item.media:credit: Gilles Sabrié for The New York Times
item.media:description: A mall in Beijing. China’s domestic economy, particularly retail sales, struggled in the third quarter.

item.title: Food Pantry Patrons Face ‘Too Much Month at the End of Their Money’
item.description: Food inflation, gas prices and cuts to federal benefits have created a “perfect storm” for food pantries, which have become vital parts of the family budget for millions of Americans.
item.dc:creator: Audra D. S. Burch
item.media:credit: Eze Amos for The New York Times
item.media:description: “People are hungry, and they are scared,” said Chris Manno, who volunteers and shops at a food pantry in Virginia.
